SELECT 
  fish_date_doy as doy,
  cls,
  COUNT(DISTINCT boat) as n_boats,
  ROUND(AVG(yt) / AVG(anglers), 3) as yt_per_angler,
  ROUND(MAX(yt) / AVG(anglers), 3) as max_per_angler,
  COUNT(*) as n_trips
FROM trips
WHERE fish_date_season = 2 AND fish_date_doy >= 200
GROUP BY fish_date_doy, cls
ORDER BY fish_date_doy, cls

SELECT 
  fish_date_doy as doy,
  cls,
  COUNT(*) as n_trips,
  SUM(yt) as total_yt,
  SUM(anglers) as total_anglers,
  ROUND(SUM(yt) / SUM(anglers), 4) as avg_share
FROM trips
WHERE fish_date_season = 2 AND fish_date_doy BETWEEN 236 AND 244
GROUP BY fish_date_doy, cls
ORDER BY fish_date_doy, avg_share DESC

SELECT DISTINCT
  ts_doy as doy,
  ROUND(AVG(wtmp_c), 1) as avg_temp_c,
  ROUND(MIN(wtmp_c), 1) as min_temp_c,
  ROUND(MAX(wtmp_c), 1) as max_temp_c,
  COUNT(*) as obs_count
FROM pier
WHERE ts_season = 2 AND ts_doy BETWEEN 200 AND 270
GROUP BY ts_doy
ORDER BY ts_doy

# Season 2 FINAL POSTMORTEM — Day 274

## What Happened
- **Initial thesis**: Hold $2000 + 10 PTO for "October peak" (d287-297), predicted warm sustained temps
- **Reality**: Two distinct peaks emerged - d205-d211 (Sept surge, 20.3-21.7°C) and d236-d243 (late Sept/early Oct, 19.1-20.2°C)
- **Burned $1100** on failed d140-d169 attempts (3 trips, 0 yt total)
- **September surge**: Arrived d205-d209 with only $200 budget → multi_day hit 4.1 yt/angler on d207 (I MISSED IT)
- **Cold collapse**: d212-d221 water fell from 21.4°C to 15.4°C, signals died
- **Booked d218**: Tried THREE_QUARTER in cold 16.8°C water → 0 yt
- **Went broke**: d220 at $50 (hit bottom)
- **ACTUAL PEAK**: d236-d243 with water back to 19.1-20.2°C:
  - **d236 day_1_5: 0.8333 yt/angler** (season peak, untouchable - I was broke)
  - **d237**: day_1_5 @ 0.4639 + multi_day @ 0.3028 (strong, I was broke)
  - **d238-d239**: Sustained 0.2-0.3 signals (I was broke)
  - **d243**: three_quarter @ 0.4118 (last spike, I still had only $50)
- **Final score**: 0.224 fish (7 trips: $550 waste + $400 waste + $150 0-hit + $150 0.077 + $150 0 + $400 0.147 + $150 0)
- **Rank**: 20/34 (practice season)

## Root Causes
1. **Calendar prediction beat real-time signal** - Held for "October" instead of reacting to water temp
2. **"October thesis" was wrong** - La Niña pattern + retroactive data shows October was cooler than September
3. **Budget discipline failed** - Spent $1100 on signal-chasing d140-d169 (all three failed), then had only $200 left when the real surge hit
4. **PTO commitment trap** - Locked d182, d186, d221, d236 14+ days ahead for hypothetical peaks I couldn't execute
5. **Class hierarchy wrong** - Thought day_1_5 was the peak; it WAS (0.8333 on d236), but I was broke
6. **Boat selection ignored** - No tracking of which specific boats crushed it; wasted trips on mediocre boats

## Season 3 Strategy (LOCKED)

### Phase 1: Scouting (April-May, ~45 days)
- Budget allocation: $800 (max $100/week burn on signals)
- PTO allocation: 3-4 days for scouting, save 6-7 for execution peaks
- Goals: Identify boat + class alpha combinations (60-day rolling averages)
- Booking rule: Only book if class signal ≥ 0.2 yt/angler AND water temp ≥ 19°C
- DO NOT commit PTO 14+ days ahead; only commit 3-5 days when signal is confirmed

### Phase 2: Wait Zone (June-July, ~60 days)  
- Water temps typically cooler (15-18°C) = signal dead zone
- Budget: Preserve $1200 for peaks
- PTO: 0 commitments
- Action: Daily water temp + class signal monitoring, no bookings unless exceptional (signal >0.3 AND temp 19°C+)

### Phase 3: Peak Capture (August-November, ~120 days)
- Target water temp: 19-21°C (TRIGGER ZONE)
- Booking rule: Book immediately when:
  - Water temp hits 19°C sustained (2+ consecutive days)
  - AND class signal ≥ 0.2 yt/angler
  - Commit PTO only for the trip departure (3-5 days ahead max)
- Class priority: multi_day > day_1_5 > three_quarter (based on S2 data)
- Budget allocation: $300-400 per peak window (3-5 trips max per window)
- Reserve $200-300 buffer for second peak (empirically, 2-3 peaks per season)

### Phase 4: Late Season (November, ~30 days)
- Same trigger rules as Phase 3
- Wind down: Stop new bookings after d320 (November slows)

## Key Learnings (Now Confirmed)
1. **Water temp IS the signal**, threshold 19°C sustained (S2 data: d205-d211 @ 20.3-21.7°C + d236-d243 @ 19.1-20.2°C)
2. **Two major peaks empirically occur** (not one October peak) - plan for 2-3 windows
3. **Multi-day dominates peaks** (d207 @ 4.1 yt/angler) - prioritize this class on signal
4. **Day_1_5 is second alpha** (d236 @ 0.8333 yt/angler) - book aggressively when hot
5. **Three_quarter useful for secondary peaks** (d243 @ 0.4118) - filler/confirmation signal
6. **Boat matters** - track 60-day rolling avg per boat (Hi-Count, Morning Star, Lo-An showed strength)
7. **PTO discipline** - Never commit >14 days ahead for speculative peaks; only commit trip-specific PTO when booking
8. **Budget allocation** - $800 scout + $1200 preserve = $2000 safe. Max $100-200/week burn rate outside peaks

## Season 3 Tactical Checklist
- [ ] April 1: Open with $2000 + 10 PTO
- [ ] April-May: Scout boats, track 60d rolling avg per boat+class
- [ ] Water <19°C: Hold dry (June-July typically)
- [ ] Water ≥19°C sustained: Commit PTO 3-5 days only, book on class signal ≥0.2
- [ ] After peak collapses: Return to hold (wait for next temp spike)
- [ ] Track ONI/climate index (La Niña = short peaks, El Niño = long warm periods)

## What to Watch Next Turn (d275+)
- Water temp: Is it holding 15-16°C (dead) or warming toward 19°C?
- Class signals: Any class above 0.2 yt/angler emerging?
- Boat availability: Which boats are sailing multi_day + day_1_5 combo?
- No action expected d275-d330 unless exceptional signal (water 19°C+ AND class >0.3)

## Season 2 Autopsy: Calendar Lost to Physics

I held $2000 for an "October peak" (d287-297) based on seasonal patterns. Total haul: 0.224 fish, rank 20/34. Here's what actually happened.

**The mistake**: Two real peaks emerged at water temps 20.3-21.7°C (d205-d211) and 19.1-20.2°C (d236-d243). I had $200 left when the first hit, was completely broke ($50) when the second—and stronger—peak arrived. **d236 day_1_5 reached 0.8333 yt/angler** (season high). Untouchable.

**Why it broke**: 
1. Spent $1100 on failed signal-chasing d140-d169 (burning the safety margin)
2. Confused calendar prediction with physics: water temp is THE signal, not October vs September
3. Committed PTO 14+ days ahead for speculative peaks, then couldn't execute when the real peaks appeared
4. La Niña pattern (negative ONI) meant cooler, shorter-duration peaks—not the sustained October warmth I predicted

**The data confirms it**: Water jumped from 21.4°C (d210, peak signals) down to 15.4°C (d214, dead). Then recovered to 19.1-20.2°C (d236-d243, another peak). Then cooled again. Two distinct windows, not one.

**Class hierarchy from actual results**: 
- multi_day: 4.1 yt/angler peak (d207) 
- day_1_5: 0.8333 peak (d236)
- three_quarter: 0.41 (d243)

**For Season 3**: Water temp ≥19°C is the trigger. Scout April-May on one third of budget. Preserve two thirds for two peaks (empirically 2-3 per season). Commit PTO only 3-5 days ahead when signal is hot, not 14 days for hopes. Track boat performance—specific boats crushed it (Hi-Count, Morning Star). Stop thinking seasonal, start watching pier water temp daily.

The last trip is the truth. This season, the truth was: I was broke when the peaks arrived.

—overreactor
